key_moments.speaker: presidenta
key_moments.text: The war in the Middle East has led to a sharp increase in energy prices, pushing up inflation and weighing on economic sentiment.

key_moments.speaker: presidenta
key_moments.text: Inflation rose to 3.0 per cent in April, from 2.6 per cent in March and 1.9 per cent in February.

key_moments.speaker: presidenta
key_moments.text: The risks to the growth outlook are to the downside.

key_moments.speaker: presidenta
key_moments.text: We still have abundance of liquidity.

briefing:
The ECB kept its key interest rates unchanged. The Hawk & Dove stance index rates the press conference as slightly hawkish: it ranks at the 69th percentile of the 52 press conferences held since December 2019, up from the 67th percentile at the previous meeting on 19 March 2026. The monetary policy statement ranks at the 67th percentile and the answers in the Q&A at the 67th.

The ECB expects the euro area economy to show some momentum, but the economic outlook is highly uncertain and will depend on how long the war in the Middle East lasts [1]. The war in the Middle East has caused significant volatility in global financial markets, and overall financial conditions remain tighter than before the war [2]. The ECB highlights the urgent need to strengthen the euro area economy while maintaining sound public finances, and fiscal responses to the energy price shock should be temporary, targeted, and tailored [3].

The risks to the growth outlook are to the downside, and the war in the Middle East remains a downside risk to the euro area economy, adding to the volatile global policy environment [4]. The risks to the inflation outlook are to the upside, and if energy prices were to rise by more and for longer than currently expected, euro area inflation would increase further [5].
